newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on port strike.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, nearbys up on port strike.

text.p: CBOT soybeans ended mixed on Tuesday with nearbys gaining strength late on short covering and on reports a strike at Brazil's Santos port could escalate to other ports, traders said.
"The head of the port in Paranagua went to Santos for a meeting so if it escalates it could stop exports," a floor source said.

Stevedores at Brazil's Santos port are on strike and the stoppage is preventing three vessels waiting to unload wheat and load soybeans from docking at public terminals. Union officials were deciding whether to call a national strike.
Soybeans opened lower and struggled much of the session on rumors two U.S. commercial firms planned to import 1.5 million to 2.0 million bushels of Brazilian soybeans.
But Brazilian trade sources downplayed the rumors, saying they could not confirm any new business. U.S. cash traders also expressed doubts, saying U.S. prices were not high enough to attract imports.
"I penciled in the numbers and unless somebody has some really cheap freight, it just doesn't work," a trader said.
Soybeans ended three cents per bushel higher to 3-1/4 cents lower with May up three at $8.36.
On the day, funds sold at least 10 million bushels of soybeans. Refco Inc sold four million July, Smith Barney sold 1.5 million July and Griffin Trading sold one million May and 1.5 million July.

Commercials were mostly on the buy side. Cargill Inc bought 1.5 million bushels May and one million July while Continental Grain, FCC and Produce Grain each bought one million bushels July, pit sources said.
Refco Inc spread two million bushels July/November at $1.29 to $1.30, premium July and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp spread one million May/November at $1.23.
In options trade, O'Connor and Co sold 450 May $9.00 calls at 1/4 cent and Produce Grain bought 350 July $10.50 calls at 3-1/2 to 3-1/8 cents.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 61,469 contracts.
